newsitem.title: USA: Rivlin, others to testify to Congress on July 23.
newsitem.headline: Rivlin, others to testify to Congress on July 23.

text.p: Federal Reserve Vice Chair Alice Rivlin is expected to testify on the economy to the House Banking Committee on July 23, a committee spokesman said on Monday.
Rivlin's testimony will come one day after central bank Chairman Alan Greenspan presents the Fed's semi-annual economic report to Congress before a House Banking subcommittee.

Fed Governor Laurence Meyer and New York Fed President William McDonough are expected to join Rivlin at the hearing. The panel also expects to hear testimony from academics, Wall Street experts and business and labor representatives.
Democratic Party lawmakers, critical of Greenspan's management of interest rate policy, had pressed for a second day of hearings to obtain differing views of the central bank's stance.
House Banking Committee Chairman Jim Leach, Republican of Iowa, also wants to have a broader view of Fed policy and agreed to the second day of talks.
